messages.subject: Package not available for R 3.3.0 -- How to Update
messages.subject_clean: Package not available for R 3.3.0 -- How to Update
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

I'm pretty new to packages, so bear with me if I'm missing something obvious.

I created a package of personal functions (we'll call it "caitlin"), which seemed to be working great until the R update. Since then, I can't load my package. I've tried:

library(devtools)
install.packages("caitlin")

which returns a warning which says "package 'caitlin' is not available (for R version 3.3.0).

Are there steps to take when R updates to update your package along with it? I've tried running document() in the "caitlin" folder (which loads all of my functions so that I can use them without properly loading the package), but would appreciate advice on this step of package development/use.

Thanks,
Caitlin

messages.body_plain:

in the package project (or if you're using RStudio, press cmd + shift
+ b)

Hadley

messages.subject: package dependencies not being installed
messages.body_plain:
Hi, I am hoping someone can help me out. I have written a package (pathtrackr) and pushed it to github. It relies on several other packages which I listed under Imports in the DESCRIPTION file, but when the package is installed it is not installing the other packages it relies on. Even if these are individually installed with install.packages(), when I call my package with library(), it does not load those packages even though they are installed.

I was able to get it to work by changing Imports to Depends, but from what I understand this is not best practice. Is there a better way to fix this or perhaps I am missing something from my DESCRIPTION or NAMESPACE file?

Thanks in advance for any help.

messages.subject: How to get install() in devtools to look for dependencies in several .libPaths
messages.subject_clean: How to get install() in devtools to look for dependencies in several .libPaths
messages.body_plain:
Hi

Is it possible to make install() look for dependencies in other .libPaths() directories before deciding to install them?

My .libPaths() setup is as follows: The first directory-path in .libPaths() is where I install my own packages and packages not on CRAN., while the second directory-path contains a lot of common packages from CRAN.

My own package depends on quite a few other packages. I wish to install it in the first directory-path in .libPath(), but I do NOT want to re-install packages which I already have installed in the second directory-path in libPaths().

When running R CMD INSTALL package from the command line, only packages not found in the second (or first) directory-path are installed (in the first one). This is the desired behavior. When running devtools install() or install_github all packages which are not found in the first directory-path are installed even if they are already installed in the second one. Look and testing various input arguments does not seem to fix this behavior.

Does anyone know whether it is possible to accomplish the command line behavior with devtools-install?
